over: export activeContext from household-recipes.ts and import it
because: every other server module (meal-plan.ts, grocery.ts, household/preferences.ts) carries its own verbatim 5-line copy already -- matching that precedent keeps one idiom repo-wide instead of making randomizer.ts the one module that imports session logic from a sibling feature module

chose: build every §4.2/§4.4/§4.6 predicate as a raw sql<boolean> fragment, applied via .where(fragment)
over: Kysely's typed eb(ref,op,val)/eb.exists(...) builder shared across box and corpus scope queries via an any-widened ExpressionBuilder<DB,any>
because: measured: widening ExpressionBuilder's TB to any to share one predicate function across the box join (hm/h/hr/r) and the bare corpus scan (r only) breaks Kysely's operand-value type inference on every 3-arg eb(ref,op,val) call -- verified by compiling, 7 TS2345 errors. Expression<SqlBool> from the sql tag carries no TB at all, so .where(fragment) type-checks identically against both query shapes with zero any anywhere in the predicate layer

chose: label all 5 randomizer facet dimensions (cuisine/diet/allergen/meal_type/spice_level) from one bounded recipe_vocab lookup, scoped to exactly the slugs found present in scope
over: reusing lib/recipe-tags.ts's private per-dimension label maps (humanize/SLUG_LABELS/ALLERGEN_NOUNS/SPICE_LABELS), which would require exporting them from a file outside this task's owned-files list
because: recipe_enrichment.ts's own module doc explicitly names this exact case (a caller needing the full grid must do its own bounded join against recipe_vocab, scoped to the slugs it knows are present) as the sanctioned alternative to the sparse per-recipe read; recipe_vocab already carries label text for all 5 dimensions (verified against migrations 1785300000000/1787679680100/1787783591746), so one authoritative source replaces what would otherwise be a second, hand-maintained label table

over: add an invariant or boundary claim that the change does not require
because: readRandomizerPool is a read-only query surface (no new table, no write) whose safety-critical properties are already pinned elsewhere: authorization is householdScopedQuery's existing membership-join invariant (reused, not reimplemented), the allergen-exclusion-is-not-a-safety-claim rule is the same one lib/recipe-tags.ts already enforces structurally (only contains/may_contain produce a filter match, asserted directly in randomizer.db.test.ts's allergen-asymmetry test), and every user value is bound via Kysely parameters / the sql tag (never interpolated) including the escapeLikePattern-escaped ILIKE text. The new surface is additive DTOs + one query function; nothing here changes an existing contract or introduces a new one worth a standalone anchor beyond the db-test suite that already pins the behavior.
